scale.2: Experimenting: some pilots and awareness, no common approach
scale.3: Formalising: policy, ownership and repeatable practice in place
scale.4: Scaling: several AI solutions in production, measured and governed
scale.5: Transforming: AI is part of how the company plans, works and competes

items.question: AI ambition is linked to named business goals
items.evidence: The board asked for 'an AI plan'; no goals or KPIs attached. The 2027 business plan names margin pressure and doc desk hiring problems, not AI.

items.question: An executive sponsor owns AI and has a budget
items.evidence: The CEO sponsors informally; no budget line. IT funds tool trials from its own budget.

items.question: AI initiatives are managed as one portfolio
items.evidence: Three unconnected experiments found (sales ChatGPT prompts, a customs Excel macro with an AI add-in, a warehouse vendor demo). Nobody had an overview.

items.question: Value is measured against a baseline
items.evidence: Doc desk volumes are counted per month; handling time and error rates were never measured before the discovery time study.

items.question: There is a view on partners and buy versus build
items.evidence: IT prefers the TMS vendor's roadmap; operations wants faster results. No criteria to decide.

items.question: Data domains have named owners
items.evidence: Customer and location master data are edited by whoever needs a change. No owner for document data.

items.question: Core master data is of usable quality
items.evidence: Sample of 200 customer records: 14% duplicates, 9% missing VAT or EORI.

items.question: Documents are available digitally
items.evidence: 90% of documents arrive as PDF by e-mail; the rest is scanned at the desk. Archive in the TMS document store, 7 years.

items.question: Labelled historical data exists to evaluate AI
items.evidence: None before the pilot. The pilot built the first labelled sets (2 x 220 documents).

items.question: Core systems can be reached through APIs
items.evidence: The TMS has an import API for bookings, undocumented for documents; the ERP only exports files overnight.

items.question: Cloud platform and identity are in place
items.evidence: Microsoft 365 and Entra ID for all staff; one Azure subscription used for backups.

items.question: Staff have sanctioned AI tools
items.evidence: No approved tool; the staff survey shows 38% use public chatbots for work, including with customer data.

items.question: An AI orchestration layer exists (model access, prompts, logging, evaluation)
items.evidence: None. Each experiment calls its own tool directly.

items.question: Systems are monitored in a way AI can plug into
items.evidence: Infrastructure monitoring exists; no application or business-level monitoring.

items.question: Security baseline is mature
items.evidence: ISO/IEC 27001 certified for IT services and customs data since 2024; supplier assessments are done, but not for AI services.

items.question: An AI policy says what is allowed
items.evidence: No AI policy. The acceptable-use policy predates generative AI.

items.question: AI systems are inventoried and classified (EU AI Act)
items.evidence: No inventory. The three experiments were found during interviews.

items.question: Human oversight and accountability are designed in
items.evidence: Four-eyes checks exist for customs declarations; no rules for AI output.

items.question: Privacy reviews (GDPR, DPIA) are routine
items.evidence: External DPO; DPIAs done for CCTV and telematics. Process exists, never applied to AI.

items.question: Vendor and model risk is managed
items.evidence: Supplier register exists; no criteria for data use, retention or model changes at AI vendors.

items.question: Staff understand what AI can and cannot do (AI literacy)
items.evidence: No training. Survey: 61% expect AI to 'replace jobs at the desk', 22% feel confident using it.

items.question: There are internal AI champions
items.evidence: Two enthusiasts (customs, sales) experimenting on their own time.

items.question: Product ownership exists for digital solutions
items.evidence: IT acts as order-taker; no business product owners.

items.question: Technical skills to run AI solutions are available
items.evidence: IT team of six: infrastructure and ERP support; one developer with Python and API experience.

items.question: The works council is involved early
items.evidence: Good relationship; informed about telematics after the fact in 2023, which still causes friction.

items.question: Core processes are documented
items.evidence: Work instructions per customer in Word files on a shared drive, 340 files, a third older than 3 years.

items.question: Process KPIs are measured
items.evidence: Volumes and on-time delivery measured; handling time, rework and error cost not.

items.question: Exceptions are handled in a defined way
items.evidence: Exceptions go to whoever is free; no categories, no log.

items.question: There is a change management practice
items.evidence: TMS go-live in 2014 remembered as painful; no change approach since.

items.question: Teams improve their own work
items.evidence: Monthly operations meeting with improvement actions; strong pragmatism on the floor.
